sentences.text:
Author: U. Durga Prasad Rao
Bench: U. Durga Prasad Rao
 Hon'Ble Sri Justice U. Durga Prasad Rao
 Criminal Petition No.5310 Of 2019
Order:

The petitioners/A1 to A3 seek to quash the proceedings against them in Crime No.135 of 2019 of Ulavapadu Police Station, Prakasam District, registered for the offences under Sections 273, 188,
328 r/w 34 of IPC and Sections 58, 59 and 63 of Food Safety and Standards Act (for short, 'FSS Act').

2. The allegations against the petitioners briefly are that on 28.08.2019 at 05.00 hours, when the complainant conducted vehicle check at Veerepalli Junction, NH-16, Ulavapadu Mandal,
intercepted the Ashok Leyland Mini truck bearing No.AP 27TY 3735 and found the banned tobacco products in the said vehicle and on interrogation, all the accused confessed to have been engaged in the business of prohibited tobacco products, seized the same, registered F.I.R. for the offences stated supra.
3.

Learned counsel for petitioners while denying the FIR allegations would submit that even if the prosecution case is accepted to be true, tobacco products would not fall within the definition of Section 3(j) of FSS Act and therefore, the police are not authorized to register the crime, investigate and file charge sheet and therefore, registration of the FIR is contrary to the provisions of FSS Act.
He relied upon the order of this Court in Crl.P.Nos.3731 of 2018 and batch, dated 27.08.2018.
As can be seen, in the said common order a learned Judge of this Court allowed the criminal petitions and quashed the offences punishable under Indian Penal Code and FSS Act.

4. Following the above order and for the reasons recorded therein, this criminal petition is allowed and the proceedings initiated against the petitioner under Sections 273, 188, 328 r/w 34 of IPC and Sections 58, 59 and 63 of FSS Act.
As a sequel, miscellaneous petitions pending, if any, in this case shall stand closed.
